skill.name: shadcn-component-boundaries

skill.summary: Separate registry primitives, reusable product components, and feature components with clear placement and dependency rules.

content.value_statement: Mixing product behavior with registry primitives makes component placement unclear and registry updates harder to manage. This skill guides alias resolution, ownership classification, and component placement with one-way dependencies.
actual_capabilities: Guide component path resolution from components.json aliases or an installed shadcn skill's project-context command.
Classify components as registry primitives, reusable product components, feature components, or route compositions.
Place reusable product wrappers in common and feature-owned components in feature folders or feature colocation.
Check that imports follow the feature-to-common-to-ui dependency direction.
Guide semantic token usage and distinguish layout classes from visual variants when shadcn lint rules are configured.
Report ownership classification, final paths, and dependency direction for components created or moved.
limitations: Provides agent instructions and examples, not a standalone scanner, refactoring program, or automated test suite.
Requires project configuration or existing shadcn tooling to resolve actual component directories.
Does not install or configure shadcn lint rules; lint enforcement depends on the project's existing setup.
Does not define framework-specific route paths or replace functional, accessibility, and integration testing.

use_cases.title: Place New Product Components
use_cases.description: Classify a shared confirmation button and a billing-only table before choosing their component directories.

use_cases.title: Protect Registry Component Boundaries
use_cases.description: Review wrappers and variants so product behavior stays outside registry primitives during component maintenance.

use_cases.title: Review Component Architecture

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Component Location
prompt_templates.prompt: Use shadcn-component-boundaries to classify [component] in this project. Resolve component aliases and recommend its final path and allowed dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Shared Wrapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [shared product component] using existing shadcn primitives. Resolve aliases, place product behavior outside ui, and report ownership, final path, and dependency direction.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component scope] against shadcn-component-boundaries. Identify misplaced product components and reverse imports, then propose specific moves with ownership classifications and final paths.

prompt_templates.title: Promote a Feature Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [feature component] for reuse by [second feature]. Remove feature-specific behavior, resolve aliases, move shared behavior to common, and check imports and configured styling rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: changing reuse scope across features.

output_examples.input: Where should an app-wide ConfirmButton wrapping Button and AlertDialog go when aliases resolve to src/components and src/components/ui?
output: Dependency direction: common imports ui primitives; ui must not import the wrapper.

output_examples.input: Where should a billing-only InvoiceTable go when the components alias resolves to src/components?
output: Dependency direction: billing may use common components and ui primitives; neither lower layer may import billing.

output_examples.input: Several features need the same new appearance for a registry Button.
output: Ownership: registry primitive with a shared visual variant.
Final path: the existing Button file in the resolved ui directory.
Add a variant to the primitive rather than creating a styled copy in common.
Keep product behavior outside ui and retain one-way imports.

best_practices: Resolve aliases before creating or moving components; do not assume a components or src/components directory.
Classify ownership and reuse scope first, then keep product behavior outside registry primitives.
Report final paths and verify one-way imports after every component creation or move.
anti_patterns: Putting product wrappers, domain behavior, or feature sections inside the registry ui directory.
Importing feature or common components from registry primitives.
Duplicating a registry primitive for styling instead of using a shared variant and semantic tokens.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when creating, moving, wrapping, or reviewing UI components in a project that uses shadcn.

faq.question: Does it require a fixed component directory?
faq.answer: No. It resolves components and ui aliases from components.json or uses an installed shadcn skill's project-context command.

faq.question: Where do reusable product components belong?
faq.answer: Place them under common in the resolved components directory. Keep feature-owned components in a named feature folder or colocated with their feature.

faq.question: Can registry primitives contain product behavior?
faq.answer: No. Keep product behavior in wrappers outside ui. Shared visual variants may be added to the registry primitive.

faq.question: Does this skill provide automatic lint enforcement?
faq.answer: No. It explains the boundary enforced by shadcn/no-restyle when @shadcn/lint is already configured.

faq.question: What should the agent report after a change?
faq.answer: It should state each created or moved component's ownership classification and final path, then confirm the dependency direction holds.
